reason: All four pins were fully read and matched their hashes, and all eight quoted excerpts verified. Both dated merchant lists have the same 29 codes. The receipt correctly preserves the opposing May acceptance guide and November overview capture claims with their route limitations. The findings overstate the novelty of capability activation, and Q1 needs the documented merchant and Connect enablement mechanics and two material UI exclusions.
required_changes: Correct the finding that the November overview adds activation state. The May overview already instructs full-Dashboard connected accounts to enable MobilePay in Payment methods and tells readers to check mobilepay_payments is active through Accounts API or webhooks (old raw lines 125-129). November retains that active check and explicitly names the Capabilities API request for connected accounts without full Dashboard access (new raw lines 149-151). In Q1 state these roles with the exact capabilities.mobilepay_payments state check, and include the separate front-end integration prerequisite to enable MobilePay in Dashboard Payment methods (new raw lines 209-213 and old raw lines 102-115). Preserve approval/status boundaries and avoid implying that the active-state check is new.

Make the November UI exclusion discoverable in Q1. The overview supports the Payment Element and rules out Express Checkout Element and Payment Method Messaging Element (new raw lines 124-132). Naming only the Checkout Sessions and PaymentIntents API families leaves the reader unable to distinguish supported Payment Element use from unsupported Express Checkout or messaging, a concrete integration selection decision. Keep the capture conflict and API-specific prerequisites as already recorded.

source_assessment_decisions.reason: The update and reciprocal capture warning are supported. Retain the May and November activation evidence with its distinct scopes and surface November's explicit unsupported UI choices alongside the product and API matrix.
